info.title: FinSight API
info.description: FinSight RPC API — every command is POST /api/rpc/{cmd} with a JSON object body. The OpenAPI file is the contract for the generated TypeScript client.

post.summary: Structured explanations of every active goal's projected completion — one per
post.description:
goal, keyed `goal:{id}` — from the same ETA the plan and the Copilot use. A
goal with no monthly contribution honestly withholds a date instead of
inventing one.

(Debt-payoff explanation is produced by the same-shaped
`finsight_agent::finance::explain_debt_payoff`, surfaced through the Copilot's
`explain_metric` tool — the debt payoff order has no dedicated screen to hang
an "explain" affordance on, so it isn't exposed as a standalone command.)

post.summary: Real implementation as of Phase 4 (previously 501'd — dialog-only).
Real implementation as of Phase 4 (previously 501'd — dialog-only).
One number for passive "needs attention" surfaces — the installed PWA's icon
post.description:
badge (Badging API), and any future glanceable indicator.

This calls the SAME five command bodies the Inbox screen sums for its header
count instead of re-deriving the total in SQL. That is the whole point: there
is exactly one definition of "an inbox item", so the badge and the screen
cannot drift apart when a sixth source is added later — whoever adds it to
the Inbox necessarily adds it here too.

Runs sequentially rather than via `try_join!`: each call borrows a pooled
blocking connection, and a badge refreshed on a slow poll is not worth
occupying five pool slots at once on a multi-user server.

AcceptCategoryProposalRequest.description:
The user agrees with the proposed category. Writes it as if the user had
typed it into the transaction-edit drawer — the write is a `source='user'`
categorization from this point on, not an unreviewed AI guess.

apr_pct.description:
Debt fields, meaningful only for Credit/Loan-type accounts (shown
conditionally in the UI, mirroring `apy_pct` for Savings). Together
these let a Credit/Loan account fully replace the standalone
liability-tracking model: a debt is just an account with a negative
balance and these optional details, not a separate entity.

post_promo_apr_pct.description:
The rate that takes over once the promo ends. `None` alongside a set
expiry means the user recorded that the rate WILL change but not to
what — a real state that must be surfaced as unknown, never silently
projected as 0%.

promo_apr_expires_on.description:
ISO date a promotional rate ends. `None` means `apr_pct` is permanent.
See [`effective_apr_pct`] — `apr_pct` always means "the rate right now",
which is why adding a promo needs no rewrite of existing data.

AccountBalanceTimeline.description:
A reconstructed balance curve for one account, derived from its opening
anchor plus cleared transaction activity.

currentCents.description: Balance at the end of the series — the reconstruction's answer for today.

earliestTxnDate.description:
Earliest cleared transaction *included in this curve*. History cannot
reach back further, so a peak before it would be invisible.

points.description:
End-of-day balance for each day the account saw activity, ascending.
Empty when the account is not reconstructable.

reconstructable.description:
False when the balance cannot be honestly derived from the ledger. See
[`AccountBalanceTimeline::skip_reason`] for which case applies.

skipReason.description:
Why reconstruction was refused, phrased for a human (or a model) to
relay. `None` when `reconstructable` is true.

AccountOwner.description:
One (account, member) ownership pair with the member's explicit share, if
any. The full list lets the UI derive sole/joint badges and per-member
net-worth attribution in one query. `share_bps` None = equal split.

balance_known.description:
False when `balance_cents` is just the untouched account-creation seed
value and the account has transaction activity that could have moved
the real balance since then. The UI must not present `balance_cents`
as a trustworthy current balance when this is false.

balance_source.description:
Source of the snapshot `balance_cents` came from: `simplefin` (bank-
reported), `manual` (legacy user-stamped), `derived` (computed from
opening + activity), or `seed` (untouched opening). Lets the UI show the
balance's basis — "synced", "estimated from your transactions", etc.

ActionItem.description: A single prioritized action item in the Financial Inbox.

actionRoute.description: Frontend route the CTA navigates to (e.g., "/transactions").

amountCents.description: Optional monetary amount in cents (e.g., bill amount).

badgeCount.description: Optional count for badge display (e.g., number of uncategorized txns).

id.description: Stable ID for this item — used as React key and for deduplication.

AddCategoryExampleRequest.description:
Attach an exemplar description to a category, keyed by the category's
stable id (so it rides through renames). Idempotent per (category, text).

`source_txn_id` is an optional provenance breadcrumb for an "add this
transaction as an example" affordance; the example survives that
transaction being deleted.

AddRestorationLegRequest.description: Attribute money that has gone back into the pot.

amountCents.description: None → account has no known balance; renderer shows `badge` instead.

AgentAccountsOverviewBlock.description:
The user's accounts.

SERVER-RENDERED: the system prompt asks the model for a bare
`{"kind":"accountsOverview"}` — no rows, balances, title, or badges — and
`synthesize_accounts_overview` fills all of it from the ledger, so a balance
can be neither invented nor omitted. `rows` is therefore `#[serde(default)]`:
the requested emission genuinely has no `rows` key on the wire, and without
the default it died on `missing field "rows"` before hydration could run.

AgentCategoryReviewQueueBlock.description:
The categorization review queue (issue #94), as a Copilot block.

SERVER-RENDERED: the model emits only `{"kind":"categoryReviewQueue"}` and
every field below is rebuilt from `category_proposals` in
`hydrate_response_blocks`. Both fields therefore default — a thin emission
must survive `parse_response_blocks`, which runs BEFORE hydration, or the
block would be dropped before it ever got its data.

pendingCount.description: Total pending proposals — may exceed `items.len()`, which is capped.

AgentClarificationBlock.description:
A question the Copilot must have answered before it can continue.

One block covers all three shapes deliberately, so the interaction reads as a
single feature rather than two: `options` empty means free text only; with
options, `multi_select` picks single- vs multi-choice. Free text stays
available either way, so the user is never trapped by an option set that
lacks their answer.

clarificationId.description: Correlates an answer back to the question that prompted it.

referenceType.description:
What kind of thing the question is about — the model names it so the
server knows what to enumerate. `"account"` today; unknown or absent
values ground to nothing and the block degrades to its free-text mode,
which is why this is optional rather than an enum.

The model naming the type is deliberate. Inferring it by pattern-
matching the question text would be a heuristic keyed on the wrong
signal — the same shape as reading intent out of model prose, which is
how confidently-wrong answers get built.

AgentClarificationOption.description:
One grounded choice in a clarification. Filled by the SERVER from real data
— never by the model, which may only choose the question. A model-invented
option could name an account the user does not have, and clicking it would
produce a confidently wrong answer.

hint.description:
Optional secondary line — a balance, a date, whatever disambiguates two
similarly-named entities.

id.description:
Stable identifier (e.g. an account id) so the answer resolves to a real
entity rather than being re-matched from its label.

amountDisplay.description: Presentational delta string, e.g. "+$213/mo" (bounded short string).

AgentNavigationTarget.description:
A screen the user can jump to in order to *see* a change the agent made.

Always an offer rendered as a link — never an automatic redirect. Yanking
someone out of a conversation mid-thread is worse than making them click.

Built from executed action payloads (which carry real entity ids) rather
than from model-authored prose, so the destination is always a screen that
exists and an entity that was actually touched.

AgentReviewMonth.description:
A month in a spending review.

Every data-bearing field is `#[serde(default)]` because this block is
SERVER-RENDERED: the system prompt tells the model to emit only `period`, a
`summary`, and `actions`, and `synthesize_spending_review` computes the rest
from the ledger. Without the defaults, the emission the prompt asks for fails
typed deserialize on `missing field "label"` and is dropped before hydration
ever runs — so only a model that DISOBEYS and invents numbers gets rendered,
the exact inversion server synthesis exists to prevent.

period.description:
`YYYY-MM` join key. The model supplies this (which months to review);
the server keys on it to compute label/spentCents/categories from core.

AgentReviewQueueItem.description: One outstanding categorization suggestion, as shown in the Copilot.

amountCents.description: None when the transaction row could not be resolved.

applied.description:
Whether the proposed category was ALREADY written to
`transactions.category_id` when the proposal was recorded. This is a
different axis from the review status and the card must not collapse
them: `applied` says whether budgets are already counting it, the
pending status says whether a human has weighed in.

AgentTxnSearchQuery.description:
The search filters that produced a transaction table, carried on the block
itself so the "Export as CSV" action can re-run the exact same query. The
model never populates this — it's attached server-side from the turn's
`search_transactions` tool call (see `copilot_chat.rs`), so the block is
self-describing and the export never depends on message structure.

ApplyCounterpartyVerdictToSimilarRequest.description:
Apply one counterparty verdict to every undecided transaction matching a
counterparty pattern (from [`UnresolvedCounterpartyDto::pattern`] or
`TransferVerdictResult::similar_pattern`). One decision clears a whole
person's e-transfer history from the review list.

ApplyNextMonthPlanRequest.description:
Write next month's budget assignments. The server has no native
notifications, so this body is purely the budget write.

ApplyScenarioRequest.description:
Apply the approved, applyable changes of a scenario to the active plan (#72).

The ONLY mechanically-applyable change today is a one-time amount, which
becomes a dated planned transaction (part of the plan, shown on `/recurring`).
Idempotent: the created transaction is tagged with the scenario id, so a
re-apply detects it and skips rather than duplicating. Aggregate deltas and
goal mentions are never written — they remain recommendations. The scenario
itself is never mutated: applying records a decision, it doesn't consume it.

ApplyScenarioResult.description: The outcome of applying approved scenario changes to the plan (#72).

applied.description: Changes written to the plan (a planned transaction was created).

skipped.description: Approved-but-not-written changes, with why (unsupported, or already applied).

AssetOwner.description:
One (asset, member) ownership pair — the manual-asset analogue of
[`AccountOwner`].

createdAt.description: File modified time, RFC3339. Empty when unavailable.

BalanceAnchorQuality.description:
How trustworthy the *level* of a reconstructed balance curve is.

A reconstruction is `opening + Σ(cleared activity)`, so its SHAPE (when the
balance rose and fell, and therefore when it peaked) is correct regardless of
the anchor. Its LEVEL is only as good as that opening figure.

BaselineSummary.description:
A compact view of the baseline a scenario was computed against, for display
and for showing the user what moved when a scenario goes stale.

BudgetEnvelope.description: One category's budget + actual for a month.

budgetCents.description: Budget set by user for the current month (0 = not budgeted this month)

carryoverCents.description:
Running (budgeted − spent) carried in from prior months, anchored at the
category's first-ever budgeted month. Positive = unspent rolling forward,
negative = accumulated overspend.

BudgetHold.description:
One month's hold — amount parked for next month.

Money parked in `month` reduces that month's `to_budget` (`income - budgeted - hold`)
and is added to `available_funds` for the following month as income-like.
This mirrors Actual's `Hold` primitive: an auditable, reversible store of
"not yet assigned" rather than silently inflating a category.

belowBuffer.description: Whether the projected balance is below the safety buffer this day.

burnCents.description: The day's share of everyday variable spend (<= 0).

eventNetCents.description: Net of the dated events landing on this day.

CashflowEvent.description:
A single dated cash movement. `amount_cents` is signed: positive inflow,
negative outflow.

confidence.description:
Detection confidence for recurring-derived events (0..1); `None` for
user-entered planned/hypothetical events, which aren't guesses.

dailyBurnCents.description: Everyday variable spend spread per day (magnitude, >= 0).

firstBreachDate.description: First day the projected balance drops below the buffer, if any.

reliable.description:
False when there's too little history (or no known balance) for the
forecast to be trusted as precise. Consumers must say so, not imply rigor.

safeToSpendCents.description:
The conservative amount safe to spend today: the lowest projected balance
minus the buffer, floored at zero. Spending it today lowers every later
day by the same amount, so the lowest point is the binding constraint.

upcomingEvents.description: The dated events inside the horizon, chronological, for display.

guidance.description:
Free-text guidance the user attaches so the categorizer/Copilot know when
to use this category (merchant hints, exclusions, intent).

CategoryExample.description:
A user-curated exemplar transaction description for a category.

Keyed by the category's STABLE `id`, so examples survive a rename exactly
the way `categories.guidance` does (rename touches `label` only).

`example_text` is a denormalized snapshot rather than a join through
`source_txn_id`: a factory reset wipes `transactions`, and a CSV re-import
churns transaction ids, so a pure reference would silently lose a curated
exemplar set. `source_txn_id` is provenance only — NULL means hand-typed
or the source transaction is gone (the FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`).

Nothing reads these yet. Issue #92 embeds `example_text` into a
prototype/centroid vector per category.

exampleText.description: The exemplar description text (trimmed, never empty).

sourceTxnId.description:
Optional provenance breadcrumb back to the transaction the user added
this from. NULL = hand-typed, or the transaction has since been deleted.

CategoryProposal.description:
A first-class record of an automated categorization SUGGESTION for a
transaction, decoupled from the canonical `transactions.category_id`
write it may or may not have made (see `applied`).

One LIVE row per transaction (`txn_id` is UNIQUE in the schema): a new
automated suggestion for the same transaction supersedes whatever
proposal was there before, so `status == "pending"` always means "the
current outstanding suggestion". Full per-attempt provenance already
lives in the append-only `categorizations` table (V003) — this table
exists to drive the review queue, not to be a second audit log.

applied.description:
Whether THIS proposal's category was written to
`transactions.category_id` when the row was created. Always `true`
today (the LLM pass still auto-writes canonical exactly as before);
a future ML pass could insert `applied = false` (a suggestion with no
canonical write) — the schema can express that without another
migration, even though this issue does not build the unapplied path.

candidatesJson.description:
Ranked candidate categories as a JSON array string (opaque to
finsight-core — not parsed or validated here). NULL until a
multi-candidate pass exists; today it holds the single winning
candidate for forward compatibility.

reviewedAt.description:
Set when a human resolves the proposal via accept/correct/reject.
NULL means either still pending, or auto-accepted without review
(status = "accepted" with reviewed_at = NULL is the auto case; a
human decision always stamps this).

source.description:
'llm' today; reserved for a future ML pass ('ml') per issue #87 scope —
that pass is not built in this issue.

CategoryWithSpending.description: Category with real spending aggregated from transactions.

guidance.description: Free-text categorizer/Copilot guidance the user attached.

thisMonthCents.description: Total outflow this calendar month (positive = money spent)

txnCount.description: Number of transactions categorised here this month

yearTxnCount.description: Number of transactions categorised here so far this calendar year

ChatHistoryEntry.description: A single prior turn from the conversation history for multi-turn awareness.

ClearScenarioRevisionRequest.description: Discard a scenario's revision, reverting to the original assumptions only.

CloseFlag.description:
A data-quality or subscription-change item to review at close. Mirrors an
Inbox action item (or #58 subscription changes) and carries a route to the
screen that resolves it — the close never resolves it inline.

acknowledged.description: Whether the user acknowledged this at close (frozen with the record).

CloseRestorationEnvelopeRequest.description:
Reconcile and finish. The design nags toward this rather than letting
envelopes accumulate.

ConversationMessage.description: A single message within a conversation thread.

agUiMetadataJson.description: JSON-encoded AG-UI metadata for tool calls, artifacts, approvals, and usage.

partsJson.description: JSON-encoded assistant-ui message parts. `content` remains the text fallback.

runStatus.description: Run lifecycle state for AG-UI/assistant reload semantics.

toolTrace.description: JSON-encoded array of tool names used, e.g. `["spending_by_category"]`

ConversationSummary.description: Summary of a conversation thread shown in the sidebar.

cached_tokens.description:
Prompt tokens the provider served from its cache this run, and the
total prompt tokens, summed across every turn. 0/0 unless the active
provider reports usage (OpenAI-compatible). The UI shows the cached
fraction as a chip.

missing_data.description:
Data the answer needed but could not find, each with an optional
destination where the user can supply it.

CorrectCategoryProposalRequest.description: The user picks a DIFFERENT category than what was proposed.

CounterpartyVerdict.description:
Serializable mirror of `finsight_core::repos::transactions::Verdict` —
the core enum has no serde/specta derives by design (finsight-core has no
Tauri/specta dependency), so this DTO crosses the specta boundary instead.

CustomReportParams.description: Parameters for the custom report query — filters + split.

CustomReportResult.description: Full result: grouped rows + grand total.

integrityStatus.description: "ok" when the last integrity check passed; otherwise the error rows.

pendingRestore.description: Set once a restore is staged; the app must restart to apply it.

startupSummary.description:
What the last launch's derived-data refresh actually changed
("Refreshed on launch: categorized 12 · matched 3 transfer pairs"),
empty when launch changed nothing.

startupWarnings.description: Non-fatal problems from the last startup derived-data cascade.

DigestFrequency.description:
How often to batch routine notifications into one summary instead of pushing
each individually (#69).

DriftLine.description: One "recorded then vs recomputed now" line for a completed close.

user_verdict.description:
A sticky user verdict (one_off / expected / investment) if the user has
annotated this merchant; overrides how it counts toward the "levers".

navigation.description:
Screens the user can open to see the applied changes in context.
Derived from the payloads of actions that succeeded, so these are
always real screens holding real entities. Rendered as an offer.

ExplainFinancialMetricsRequest.description:
Structured "explain this number" provenance for the decision-driving
dashboard metrics, optionally scoped to one household member. Every value is
pulled from the same `finsight-core::metrics` layer `get_financial_metrics`
reads, so an explanation can never disagree with the number shown elsewhere.
The single source of truth is shared verbatim with the Copilot's
`explain_metric` tool.

ExplainScenarioRequest.description:
Structured "explain this scenario" — the same recomputed projection the
comparison shows, described via `provenance::scenario_explanation` (its
narrative `considerations` become the tradeoffs, so this can never disagree
with the scenario card). A pre-V055 legacy row that can't be recomputed gets
the legacy variant: a withheld value with the reason, never a fabricated
breakdown.

ExportAccountCsvRequest.description:
Returns the CSV content for one account's transactions (caller downloads
it client-side — no server-side file I/O). Real implementation as of
Phase 4; previously 501'd behind a native-dialog-only Tauri command.

ExportSearchTransactionsCsvRequest.description:
Re-run the Copilot `search_transactions` query and return the matching
rows as CSV content (caller downloads it client-side). Shares
`transactions::search` with the Copilot tool so the exported rows match
exactly what the card displayed. Real implementation as of Phase 4;
previously 501'd behind a native-dialog-only Tauri command.

ExportTransactionsCsvRequest.description:
Returns the CSV content for transactions matching a filter (caller
downloads it client-side — no server-side file I/O). Real implementation
as of Phase 4; previously 501'd behind a native-dialog-only Tauri command.

currency.description:
The currency every `_cents` field above is denominated in, derived from
live accounts and manual assets rather than from a display preference —
a preference goes stale the moment holdings change. `None` only when
there are no accounts or manual assets yet.

safetyBasisSpanDays.description:
Days of history behind the safety basis, so the UI can say WHY a figure
is withheld instead of showing a bare dash.

unconvertedHoldings.description:
Money held in other currencies, never converted and never folded into
the totals above. Non-empty means every figure here is a partial view,
and the UI must label it as such rather than render a bare number.

FinancialPhilosophyDto.description:
The user's stated philosophy, as the UI reads and writes it.

Strings rather than enums on the wire so an older client that sends an
unrecognised value degrades to the default instead of failing the request —
a preference is never worth erroring over.

highInterestAprPct.description:
Derived, read-only: the APR at or above which debt is treated as
high-interest. Surfaced so the Settings screen can show the
consequence of the choice rather than just its name.

GetAccountBalanceTimelineRequest.description:
Reconstruct an account's balance curve from its ledger, with the peak and
trough over the requested window. `since` is an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` date; omit
it for all-time.

Unlike [`list_account_balance_history`], which reads the sparse stored
snapshots, this derives every point — so it can answer "when was this account
at its highest" rather than "which recorded day was highest".

GetCashflowForecastRequest.description:
Project the liquid balance forward `horizon_days` (default 30, clamped
7–90), optionally against a safety `buffer_cents` and a hypothetical one-off
outflow. Returns the daily trajectory, the lowest point, the first day it
breaches the buffer, the conservative safe-to-spend, upcoming dated events,
and data-quality warnings.

GetMonthCloseRequest.description:
The close for a given month: live figures/flags while unopened or in
progress; the frozen record (plus drift) once completed.

GetRestorationStatusRequest.description: The three reliable numbers plus the honest ceiling, for one envelope.

priority.description:
"critical" | "high" | "normal" | "someday" — how much this goal matters,
as distinct from `sort_order`, which is only where the card sits.

HouseholdMember.description:
A person in the household (single user, partner, family member, roommate).
Accounts are owned by zero or more members; 2+ owners = a joint account.

isSelf.description:
True for the one member who operates this install (the "self"). At most
one member is self; drives "my finances" views and self-transfer
recognition. Zero members ⇒ no self, behaves as a solo household.

ImportCsvRequest.description:
Import a CSV file, running the deterministic post-import cascade
(categorization, transfer pairing, anomaly refresh, net-worth refresh) and
enqueuing the AI categorizer. Progress and completion are pushed through the
`sink` (`"import-progress"` / `"import-complete"`).

ImportResult.description:
The import outcome plus what still needs a category. Surfacing the
uncategorized count (and whether the AI pass was auto-started) makes the
cloud LLM categorization a visible, informed choice rather than a silent
background enqueue.

aiCategorizationStarted.description:
True when the background AI categorizer was auto-enqueued (the
auto-categorize setting is on). When false, the UI offers an explicit
"run AI categorization" action.

builtinCategorized.description:
Rows the deterministic builtin pass categorized in this import's
cascade — shown post-import so the derived work is visible, not silent.

transfersPaired.description: Cross-account transfer pairs linked in this import's cascade.

uncategorizedAfter.description:
Uncategorized non-transfer EXPENSE rows in this account after the builtin
pass — exactly what an AI categorization run would work on.

InboxBadgeCount.description:
The "needs attention" total, broken down by source.

The breakdown fields exist so the number is debuggable — when a badge shows
"7" and the user expects "3", the caller can say which bucket the extra four
came from without re-running five queries by hand.

InvestmentSummary.description: Ledger-derived portfolio summary for one investment account.

cashCents.description:
Cash in the account: opening (seed) balance + every ledger row. Trades,
contributions, dividends, interest, and tax are all cash movements.

hasNegativeQuantity.description:
True when any symbol nets below zero — a SELL without its earlier BUYs
(partial-history import). The estimate is unreliable; warn, don't hide.

positionsValueCents.description: Σ market value of open positions at their last trade price.

withholdingTaxCents.description: All-time withholding tax, as a positive magnitude (rows are negative).

ListCategoryExamplesRequest.description:
Every exemplar for a category, oldest first.

Returns rows for ARCHIVED categories too, mirroring how `list_categories`
still returns `guidance` on an archived row — archiving hides examples from
active consumers, it does not delete them.

ListMemberBudgetEnvelopesRequest.description:
Budget-vs-actual for the current month, scoped to one household member's
share of the spend. The budgets themselves are the household's.

ListNotificationsRequest.description:
The notification history. `includeResolved=false` (default view) shows only
still-active items; held (quiet-hours) items appear here too so they're never
lost, just not pushed.

LookBackFact.description:
A single plain-language fact about how `month` went for a budgeted category,
used to open the Plan Next Month wizard. Deterministic, no LLM — the frontend
composes the sentence (and applies the user's money formatting/privacy mode)
from `kind` + `amount_cents`/`streak_months`; this never bakes a formatted
dollar string server-side.

amountCents.description: Meaningful for "over" (spent − budgeted) and "under" (budgeted − spent); 0 for "streak".

streakMonths.description: Meaningful for "streak" (consecutive zero-spend months including `month`); 0 otherwise.

MarkSubscriptionCancelledRequest.description:
Mark a detected subscription CANCELLED as of `cancelled_at` (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
Ongoing price/renewal alerts stop; a charge dated after the cancel date is
surfaced as a surprise. `label` names the service in that alert (#75).

MemberBudgetEnvelope.description:
One category's household budget alongside a single member's share of the
spend against it. The budget itself stays household-level — the issue keeps
budgets a shared pool and adds a per-person *view* of progress against it,
rather than splitting the target itself.

budgetCents.description: The household budget for this category — the same target everyone sees.

householdSpentCents.description: The whole household's spend, for "my share of our total" context.

memberSpentCents.description: This member's ownership-weighted share of that spend.

MemberNetWorth.description:
One row of the "who owns what" household net-worth split. `member_id` None is
the unassigned residual — value owned by no recorded member, i.e. by people
running their OWN separate FinSight app (the cross-user share). Member slices
plus the residual reconcile to the household total.

MetricAssumption.description: A tunable assumption that shaped the metric (e.g. the user's target rate).

MetricExplanation.description:
A complete, self-consistent explanation of one financial metric: what it
means, what produced it, what it leaves out, what it assumes, over what
period, and how far to trust it.

definition.description: One-sentence definition of what the number represents.

inputs.description: The material inputs that produced it, with their amounts where money.

key.description: Stable identifier, e.g. `"net_worth"`. Safe to switch on.

period.description: The time window the figure covers.

tradeoffs.description:
Material tradeoffs between this result and the competing option(s) — the
"why this and not the alternative" reasoning. Empty for a descriptive
metric that has no alternative (e.g. net worth); populated for a
recommendation such as a debt-payoff order or a contribution level.

warnings.description: Data-quality caveats: missing / stale / withheld / low-confidence disclosures.

MetricValue.description:
The metric's value, tagged so the UI knows how to format it and so a
withheld figure is a first-class state rather than a fabricated zero.

MetricWarning.description: One data-quality caveat: missing, stale, low-confidence, or unsupported data.

MetricWarningLevel.description: Severity of a data-quality caveat attached to a metric.

MissingDataItem.description:
Something the Copilot needed but could not find, and — where we can work it
out — where the user would go to supply it.

The Copilot deliberately withholds high-confidence debt advice when APR or
minimum-payment data is absent. That is the right call, but a block that
does not say how to unblock it reads as the app being unhelpful rather than
careful. Attaching a destination turns an honest limitation into a
completed setup step.

`action_label` and `action_path` are always set or cleared **together**: a
labelled button with nowhere to go, or a destination with no label, are
both worse than plain prose. Producers that do not know which entity is
missing data (notably the model itself, on the deep reasoning path) build
these through [`From<String>`], which leaves both `None` — the message
still renders, just without a shortcut.

actionLabel.description: Button text, e.g. "Add APR". `None` when there is nowhere to send them.

message.description: Human-readable description of what is missing.

MonthCloseSnapshot.description:
The month's key figures. Enriched over the old review snapshot with net
worth, debt, and a count of subscription price changes. Free-form goal JSON
is kept for the UI's progress list.

drift.description: Only populated for a completed close whose recorded figures now differ.

flags.description: Live flags while in progress; the frozen (acknowledged-marked) set once completed.

MonthSummary.description: One month's summary for the bar chart.

expenseCents.description: Total outflows (negative transactions), as positive cents

incomeCents.description: Total inflows (positive transactions), as positive cents

MonthTotals.description: Lightweight summary for the Today screen.

priority.description: Omitted by callers that do not care; the schema defaults apply.

Notification.description: A stored notification, as the history surface reads it.

NotificationCategory.description:
What a notification is about. Drives the per-category user preference and how
events are grouped. The string form is the stored value and the preference key.

categories.description: Every category with its current enabled state, in a stable order for the UI.

snoozeUntil.description:
A one-off "snooze until" RFC3339 instant, or null. While active it holds
individual pushes of non-critical notifications (#69). The client sets it
to `now + duration`; a past value is treated as not snoozed.

utcOffsetMinutes.description:
The client's UTC offset in minutes (`local = UTC + offset`). The client
stamps this on every save so the server can evaluate the local-time quiet
window; the user never edits it directly.

OwnerShare.description:
An owner and their explicit ownership share (basis points, 10000 = 100%) for
an account or asset. `share_bps` None ⇒ equal split with the other owners.

PathBackView.description: Everything the Path Back screen needs, in one read.

elevated_recent_months.description: How many of the 3 months before `period` were also above the band.

mixed_currency.description:
True when the ledger spans multiple currencies — the totals mix them, so
treat the verdict as approximate (parity with decompose's warning).

upper_band_cents.description: median + BAND_K robust sigmas — spend above this is "elevated".

PlanChange.description:
One proposed plan change from promoting a scenario — a suggestion for the
user to review. Most are recommendation-only; a change with `applyable=true`
can be written to the plan on explicit approval (#72).

applyable.description:
Whether this change can be mechanically applied to the plan. Only true for
changes that map to a concrete plan entity — a one-time amount becomes a
dated planned transaction. Aggregate world-assumptions (income %, monthly
spending delta) and goal mentions have no unambiguous target, so they stay
recommendations the user acts on themselves.

id.description: Stable key the apply step approves by (e.g. "one_time").

Position.description: One open position in an investment account, aggregated from Trade rows.

investedCents.description:
Net cash put into this symbol: SUM(−amount) over its trades. A closed
round trip leaves the realized P&L here as a negative (profit) or
positive (loss) residue.

lastPrice.description: Unit price of the most recent trade in this symbol (dollars).

lastTradeAt.description: Date of that most recent trade (RFC3339).

marketValueCents.description: quantity × last_price, rounded to cents. None when no price is known.

quantity.description: Net units held: SUM(quantity) over all trades (SELL rows are negative).

PreparedImportPreview.description:
A lightweight, bounded preview of what an import WOULD do — counts + a
capped error list + a staleness signature — so the UI can show
"N new · D duplicates · R to review" before the user commits to importing.
Deliberately excludes per-row decisions: those can number in the
thousands and must never cross the Tauri IPC boundary wholesale.

PriceChangeDto.description: A detected material change in a fixed-price recurring charge's amount (#58).

pct.description: Signed percent change vs the prior price.

PrivacyLevel.description:
How much sensitive detail a notification may expose. Mirrors the app's
"blur amounts" privacy concept rather than inventing a parallel model — a
push composed server-side can't consult the client's blur, so this is the
server-side equivalent.

PromoteScenarioRequest.description:
Promote a scenario into a REVIEWABLE set of proposed plan changes. This
writes nothing: it grounds each proposal in the current baseline and hands
them back for the user to approve and apply themselves.

PushDeliveryReport.description:
Outcome of a send. Reported rather than swallowed so the Settings screen can
tell "no devices registered" apart from "the push service rejected us".

expired.description:
Subscriptions the push service reported as permanently gone; these are
deleted rather than retried forever.

PushPayload.description:
The JSON body `push-sw.js` parses. Keep the field names in lockstep with it
— the contract is pinned by `ui/src/pwa/push.test.ts`.

badgeCount.description:
Lets the worker refresh the app-icon badge while the app is closed —
the one thing the foreground badge hook cannot do.

tag.description:
Collapse key: a newer message with the same tag replaces the older one
instead of stacking another line on the lock screen.

deviceCount.description: How many devices are currently registered for this user.

end.description: Local hour 0–23 it ends. Equal to `start` means "no window".

start.description: Local hour 0–23 the quiet window starts.

RanScenario.description:
A run's result together with the resolved params, so the UI can save a
scenario it ran from free text (where the params were resolved server-side).

RecurringItem.description: A recurring transaction detected from transaction history (Phase 6 redesign).

cancelledAt.description:
If the user marked this cancelled, the cancel date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); a
charge after it is surfaced as a surprise. `null` otherwise (#75).

confidence.description: 0..1 confidence this is a genuine recurring item.

feedsProjections.description:
Whether this item is confident enough to feed forward-looking
projections. Low-confidence entries stay VISIBLE — the user is the one
who can confirm or dismiss them — but do not silently move arithmetic.

isSubscription.description: True only for genuine subscriptions (not repeat purchases).

merchantKey.description:
The canonical grouping key — the handle the confirm/dismiss verdict is
keyed on (`set_subscription_verdict`).

monthlyEquivalentCents.description:
Cost per month with cadence accounted for, positive. Computed in
`finsight-core` so the UI does not re-derive the normalisation and
disagree with the budget and Copilot figures built on the same rule.

trialEndsAt.description:
If the user marked this a free trial, the date it converts (`YYYY-MM-DD`);
a heads-up fires shortly before. `null` when not a trial (#75).

verdict.description:
The user's durable verdict on this series: "confirmed" | "dismissed" |
"cancelled" | null. A dismissed series is suppressed from alerts; a
cancelled one stops ongoing alerts but flags a charge after the cancel
date (#75).

RejectCategoryProposalRequest.description:
The user dismisses the proposal without providing a replacement category.
Canonical `transactions.category_id` is left untouched (it already holds
the LLM's applied guess) — this only removes the item from the review
queue.

RemoveCategoryExampleRequest.description: Remove one exemplar by its own id. No-op if it's already gone.

counterpartyPattern.description:
Optional `%name%` pattern for the person expected to pay some of it
back. One person deliberately — see the repo docs.

openedOn.description: ISO date the money left the pot.

RestorationStatus.description:
Everything needed to say the sentence, and nothing that would need to be
asserted without evidence.

collectableCents.description:
What a person still owes, from the counterparty tab. Zero when the
envelope names nobody — an unlinked envelope has nothing collectable,
and guessing across every counterparty would produce a confident wrong
figure.

fundYourselfCents.description: What the user has to find themselves: left-to-restore minus collectable.

leftToRestoreCents.description: Original minus restored. The headline number.

restoredCents.description: Sum of everything attributed as already gone back.

stale.description: Open long enough that it should be reconciled and closed.

stillHeldBasis.description: Why the ceiling is what it is, or why there isn't one.

stillHeldCeilingCents.description:
An UPPER BOUND on what could still be sitting in the destination
account, never a claim that it is.

The naive "still remaining" figure degrades silently: withdraw in
January, flag a couple of legs, and it will still confidently report the
same number in July after six months of unrelated churn. At that point
it is not measuring anything.

The account's lowest end-of-day balance since the withdrawal is a real
bound instead — if checking dipped to $2,000 in March, the user
demonstrably is not still holding $9,500. `None` when the destination is
unknown or its balance cannot be reconstructed, which is the honest
answer rather than a guess.

ReviseScenarioRequest.description:
Revise a saved scenario's assumptions (issue #73). Stores a second set of
what-if params alongside the immutable original; the returned detail carries
the recalculated `revised_result` next to the original and current results.
Never touches the active plan, and never overwrites the original params.

RuleWithCategory.description: Rule with resolved category label and color.

acknowledgedFlagIds.description: Flag ids the user ticked as acknowledged — recorded when completing.

SaveMonthCloseRequest.description:
Advance the close lifecycle. `completed` freezes the snapshot, baseline, and
acknowledged flags; `in_progress`/`skipped` only move status + notes and
leave any prior frozen record intact (reopen keeps history; re-completing
re-freezes explicitly).

SaveScenarioRequest.description:
Save a scenario durably: capture the current baseline, re-project the params
against it, and store params + baseline + result together so the scenario
can later be recomputed, compared, and checked for staleness.

SavedScenarioDetail.description:
A saved scenario with everything needed to compare and act on it. The
`original_*` fields are exactly what was saved; `current_result`/`is_stale`
recompute it against TODAY's baseline so every compared scenario shares one
baseline (consistent by construction) while the original stays distinct.

isStale.description: Whether the current baseline differs materially from the saved one.

ScenarioPlanProposal.description:
The reviewable result of promoting a scenario. Deliberately carries NO write
path: promoting produces suggestions only, so exploration can never silently
change live budgets, goals, or debt plans.

SearchTxnQueryInput.description:
Input for [`export_search_transactions_csv`] — mirrors the Copilot
`search_transactions` tool's query shape so the exported rows match
exactly what the card displayed. Moved here from finsight-bindings in Phase 4
(was finsight-bindings-only before the export commands became transport-agnostic).

SendPushForDbRequest.description:
See `vapid_keypair_for_db` — the `Db`-only entry point, for the background
scheduler.

SendPushRequest.description:
Deliver `payload` to every device this user registered.

Never returns Err for a per-device failure: one dead subscription must not
abort delivery to the user's other devices, so failures are counted in the
report instead. A 404/410 from the push service means the subscription is
permanently gone, and the row is deleted — otherwise every future send
retries a device that will never come back.

SetCounterpartyVerdictRequest.description:
Record the user's 3-way verdict (transfer / settle-up / real spending) on
a transfer-review counterparty transaction. Sticky: survives re-imports
and categorizer re-runs.

SetSubscriptionTrialRequest.description:
Mark a detected subscription as a free TRIAL converting on `trial_ends_at`
(`YYYY-MM-DD`), or clear it with `trial_ends_at = None`. `label` is the
display name captured for the reminder. A heads-up fires shortly before the
date (#75).

SetSubscriptionVerdictRequest.description:
Set (or clear, with `verdict = None`) the user's confirm/dismiss verdict on a
detected subscription. `verdict` accepts "confirmed" | "dismissed"; any other
value (or null) clears it, so a bad string can't corrupt state.

accepted.description:
Drivers the user accepted (expected/investment) — kept in the floor,
surfaced so they can be reviewed and undone; not levers, not self-correcting.

baseline_monthly_cents.description: Your robust normal (median of the trailing months).

levers.description: The specific recurring levers to act on, ranked by size.

projected_after_levers_cents.description: Where you'd land if the one-offs lapse AND you trim every lever.

recoverable_recurring_cents.description: Recurring/emerging drivers you could trim — the levers.

self_correcting.description: The one-off drivers that lapse on their own — shown as "leave them".

self_correcting_cents.description: One-off drivers that fall off on their own — no action needed.

structural_gap_cents.description:
Present only with a target BELOW what trimming reaches: the remaining
gap is structural (a floor / fixed commitments), not more trimming.

SplitBy.description: How to slice the expense pie.

StreamCopilotMessageRequest.description:
Send a message to the Copilot within a conversation.

1. Persists the user message.
2. Runs the reasoning engine (deep-mode agent pipeline).
3. Streams the answer word-by-word via `copilot-stream-frame` frames pushed
through `sink` (a real Tauri window event on desktop, an SSE broadcast on
finsight-server).
4. Persists the assistant message and emits the `Done` frame.
5. Auto-generates a title for new conversations after the first message.

owner_member_id.description:
Household member this transaction is attributed to, overriding the
account's ownership shares for its cashflow (a personal purchase on a
joint account). None = use the account shares.

transfer_peer_account_name.description: Display name of the peer leg's account ("Transfer → Tangerine Savings").

transfer_peer_id.description:
Id of the matching leg in another account when this transaction is one
half of a paired cross-account transfer (see `categorize::pair_transfers`).

TransferVerdictResult.description:
Result of a transfer verdict: the updated transaction, plus how many other
UNDECIDED transactions share the same counterparty so the UI can offer to
apply the verdict to all of them in one click.

similarLabel.description: Human-readable counterparty ("jordan") for the offer text.

similarPattern.description:
LIKE pattern identifying the siblings (pass to
`apply_transfer_verdict_to_similar`), e.g. `%jordan%`.

TxnActivity.description:
Investment/activity metadata parsed from brokerage CSV exports
(Wealthsimple et al). Stored provider-verbatim in the six V048 columns;
`categorize::activity_implies_transfer` decides which activity types are
internal moves (Trade, MoneyMovement) vs real income/expense.

quantity.description: Signed units traded; SELL rows are negative.

unitPrice.description: Dollars at full export precision (sub-cent), NOT cents.

UnconvertedHolding.description:
A currency the user holds that these metrics are NOT denominated in.
Reported so the UI can say "also holding US$3,200, not converted" instead of
either inventing an exchange rate or silently omitting real money.

UnresolvedCounterpartyDto.description:
One counterparty's undecided transfer-like rows, netted for the grouped
review surface. Mirrors `finsight_core::repos::transactions::UnresolvedCounterparty`.

UpdateGoalPriorityRequest.description:
Set how much a goal matters and what its date commits the user to.

The two travel together because neither is meaningful to the planner alone:
a hard deadline on a `someday` goal and a `critical` goal with no date are
both coherent, and allocation needs to see the pair to order them.

Unrecognised strings fall back to the neutral defaults rather than erroring
— this is a preference, and refusing to save a goal over a bad enum value
would be a worse outcome than storing "normal".
